title: Erdős #247: Transcendence of Lacunary Sums
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #247: transcendence of lacunary binary sums Σ 1/2^{n_k} when the sequence n_k grows fast. Defines HasWeakGrowth (lim sup n_k/k = ∞) and HasStrongGrowth (super-polynomial). Proves 2^k satisfies strong growth. Axiomatizes Erdős's 1975 result: strong growth implies transcendence. Proves the conjecture (open general case) is implied by the axiom for factorial and 2^k sequences. 22 theorems, 7 definitions, 1 axiom.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: erdos_transcendence_strong — Erdős 1975: if n_k is strictly increasing with HasStrongGrowth (lim sup n_k/k^t = ∞ for all t ≥ 1), then Σ 1/2^{n_k} is transcendental over ℚ.
originalContributions: lacunarySum: Σ_{k=1}^∞ 1/2^{n_k} — the lacunary binary sum
HasStrongGrowth: lim sup n_k/k^t = ∞ for all t — stronger condition

overview.historicalContext: Erdős (1975) asked: if n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ with lim sup n_k/k = ∞, is Σ 1/2^{n_k} transcendental? He proved the stronger version (super-polynomial growth) using Liouville-type rational approximation arguments. The general case (merely lim sup → ∞) remains open. Erdős noted in 1988 these problems 'seem hopeless at present'. The sum is a binary expansion with 1s at positions n_k — its transcendence reflects the irrationality of the pattern.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: if n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ is strictly increasing with lim sup n_k/k = ∞, then Σ 1/2^{n_k} is transcendental. (Open in general; proved for super-polynomial growth by Erdős.)
overview.text: The sum Σ 1/2^{n_k} is a real number with a binary expansion having 1s at positions n_k. When gaps between consecutive positions grow fast enough, the number cannot be algebraic. The proof uses the fact that algebraic numbers of degree d satisfy |α - p/q| > c/q^d, but lacunary sums with fast-growing gaps can be approximated to any polynomial order, forcing transcendence via Liouville's theorem.
overview.proofStrategy: Define the formal infrastructure: lacunarySum, HasWeakGrowth, HasStrongGrowth. Prove key examples (2^k, k!) satisfy strong growth. Axiomatize Erdős's theorem for strong growth. Prove the conjecture follows for all super-polynomial sequences. Derive irrationality as a consequence.
keyInsights: Liouville argument: fast-growing gaps give unusually good rational approximations, forcing transcendence
2^k and (k+1)! satisfy strong growth: proved elementarily
Strong growth ↔ super-polynomial: stronger than lim sup n_k/k = ∞
Open gap: weak growth (lim sup n_k/k = ∞) may not suffice
prerequisites: Liouville transcendence theory: rational approximation obstructions
Series convergence: infinite sums in ℝ
Algebraic and transcendental numbers: Transcendental predicate

conclusion.summary: Lacunary sum transcendence formalized: HasWeakGrowth and HasStrongGrowth predicates, 2^k and k! proved to satisfy strong growth, Erdős 1975 theorem axiomatized. 22 theorems, 506 lines, 1 axiom.
conclusion.implications: The Erdős conjecture (weak growth → transcendence) remains open. The formalization provides the framework for attacking it via Liouville theory. Transcendence of specific lacunary sums like Σ 1/2^{2^k} follows immediately from the axiom.
openQuestions: Prove the full Erdős conjecture: weak growth implies transcendence
Prove the Erdős strong-growth theorem without axioms using Liouville machinery in Mathlib
Generalize to base-p lacunary sums Σ 1/p^{n_k} for prime p

crossReferences.description: Both are open Erdős problems in number theory; prime gaps and lacunary transcendence share analytic depth
